assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data were used to measure intergenerational mobility, including its geographic variation and its causal drivers such as neighbourhood exposure effects. This combines new data with a credible quasi-experimental design on a big question, and the work has had large policy and research impact. It is a close fit to the standard of data discovery plus an explanatory framework.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear intellectual centre. Hendren (neighbourhood effects, exposure-time design) and Friedman (teacher value-added, mobility atlases) are the most plausible co-recipients. Lawrence F. Katz has important earlier contributions, mainly the Moving to Opportunity work, but is credited more naturally under other bodies of work.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date from roughly 2014 to 2022 and have been replicated and extended across countries. The area is young compared with typical prizes but already has a substantial body of confirmation.
uncertainties: Whether the committee regards the programme as mature enough, given its recency
Whether the prize would be framed around mobility measurement or around the broader quasi-experimental public-economics agenda
Debate over the size of neighbourhood causal effects and over how far rank-rank measures generalise

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the China-shock studies of local labour-market adjustment changed how economists understand wage inequality, automation and trade. The work has major societal significance and fits across labour, trade and public policy.
assessment.attribution: Autor anchors both the task framework and the trade-shock work. Hanson and Dorn are co-authors of the China-shock programme. Lawrence F. Katz made foundational contributions on skill-biased change and education-technology races, but a three-person limit forces a choice, and Katz has a claim under this heading too.
assessment.maturity: The work spans about two decades. The China-shock findings have been extensively replicated and debated, and the framework is widely taught.
uncertainties: Contested identification and the scope of the China-shock effects
Who among Autor, Hanson, Dorn and Katz is most central for a three-person limit
Some of the task-model foundations (Acemoglu, Autor and others) are not in this candidate's credited set

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities (Calvo pricing, the Taylor rule, and the micro-founded synthesis in Woodford) underlies modern central-bank policy analysis. It has very large practical and theoretical influence.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is diffuse among at least eight credited names. Calvo (pricing), Taylor (rules and staggered contracts) and Woodford (the integrated framework) are the clearest foundational pillars. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets are important for the empirical and DSGE side.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of use in policy institutions. Some of the foundational work may already be partly recognised through earlier prizes in the area.
uncertainties: Choosing three among many contributors who are plausibly equal
The framework's reputation has been affected by criticism since the pandemic-era inflation
Overlap with earlier macroeconomics prizes

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm model of trade explains selection, exporting and the gains from trade, and it changed both theory and empirical trade research. It has been very influential on how trade-policy effects are understood.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the principal originator of the model. Helpman is central to the firm-level trade programme and the wider trade theory, and he is also credited in the candidate list for the political-economy trade work. Redding is a major contributor to quantitative extensions.
assessment.maturity: The model is more than two decades old and is standard in teaching and in research. Its empirical validation is wide.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier Krugman prize and with credit due to other firm-heterogeneity authors, such as Bernard, Eaton, Kortum and others not listed here
Whether Redding should be included alongside the two selected

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learning methods for heterogeneous treatment effects and debiased or double machine learning have given empirical researchers new tools for credible causal estimation with high-dimensional data. They are widely used across fields.
assessment.attribution: Chernozhukov is credited for double and debiased machine learning, which is an econometric foundation. Athey and Wager are credited for causal forests and related heterogeneous-effect methods. The methodological credit is clear, but other contributors (Imbens, Belloni, Hansen and others) may also have strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Mostly dated 2015 to 2020, so it is relatively recent. Adoption is growing quickly, but the long-run consequences are not yet fully established.
uncertainties: Recency compared with older econometrics candidates
Whether the credited set omits co-originators of the double machine learning framework
Overlap with the earlier 2021 prize on causal inference, which could affect timing

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence on reciprocity and fairness, plus the Fehr-Schmidt model of inequity aversion, changed how economists treat social preferences and incentives. The experimental evidence, together with an explanatory model, is influential in contract theory and public policy.
assessment.attribution: Fehr-Schmidt (1999) is the central formal contribution, and Fehr is the main empirical driver. Falk is an important co-contributor on experiments and field evidence. Parallel work by Bolton and Ockenfels and by Rabin is outside this credited set.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with more than 25 years of replication and extension, and a body of both support and critique.
uncertainties: Missing credit to parallel authors (Bolton-Ockenfels, Rabin)
Lab-to-field external validity
Overlap with earlier behavioural and experimental prizes

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run, archive- and tax-record-based series on top incomes and wealth created a new empirical basis for the study of inequality. This matches the 'detective work in archives' standard of building data, and it also supplied frameworks (such as capital-income dynamics) that organise the facts. Its impact on society and on the policy debate is large.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the originators of the top-income series. Zucman is credited for wealth distribution and offshore wealth. Atkinson, who is deceased, contributed to the field but cannot be awarded.
assessment.maturity: Series date back to the early 2000s and are well established. The newer wealth and offshore estimates are more contested.
uncertainties: Methodological disputes about measurement, especially of wealth and capital shares
Political salience of the work, which must not enter the assessment
Whether the explanatory framework is as strong as the data contribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Micro-data evidence that household leverage and mortgage credit expansion drove the housing boom, consumption collapse and slow recovery changed the understanding of the Great Recession. The work combines new data, credible geographic identification and a coherent explanation.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the clear joint originators. Campbell is credited for household finance more broadly and has a weaker link to this specific discovery.
assessment.maturity: The central papers date to about 2009 to 2015 and are already extensively cited and tested, though the field continues to evolve.
uncertainties: Debate about the relative roles of credit supply, expectations and demand
Whether the committee would prefer a broader macro-finance or financial-crisis prize
Ongoing replication and measurement debates
